title: The Balance Behind the Bend
endLine: Lactate builds when appearance outruns clearance, not when oxygen runs out.

scenes.tts: The first film found the ceiling. In healthy people running or cycling at sea level, oxygen delivery mainly sets it. But no one races for long at the ceiling. As the pace rises, blood lactate climbs faster. Is the muscle running out of oxygen?
scenes.narration: The first film found the ceiling. In healthy people running or cycling at sea level, oxygen delivery mainly sets it. But no one races for long at the ceiling. As the pace rises, blood lactate climbs faster. Is the muscle running out of oxygen?
scenes.caption: The first film found the ceiling. In healthy people running or cycling at sea level, oxygen delivery mainly sets it. But no one races for long at the ceiling. As the pace rises, blood lactate climbs faster. Is the muscle running out of oxygen?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 colour map: GREEN = oxygen uptake; BLUE = flow, blood and the heart; ORANGE = extraction; PURPLE = muscle; YELLOW = the question and the ceiling; RED = a caution; GREY = axes and labels. New in this film: MAGENTA = lactate; TEAL = glucose made by the liver. A small 'schematic' tag sits bottom right all film. RECAP (first two sentences): the first film's Fick rectangle appears small at top left, BLUE width labelled 'flow', ORANGE height 'extraction', GREEN area; on 'oxygen delivery mainly sets it' the BLUE width glows, then the rectangle shrinks into a corner badge and stays there. THE WORLD, built on 'no one races for long', carried all film: LEFT, a large PURPLE working thigh muscle (cartoon block of fibres, no molecular detail) with a BLUE capillary band running out of it to the right across the frame; CENTRE above the band, a tall vertical gauge labelled 'blood lactate' (MAGENTA fill, no numbers); LEFT EDGE, a GREEN uptake bar with a YELLOW dashed line above it labelled 'ceiling'; the bar fills to a level clearly below the line, labelled 'race pace' (schematic). Ambient: BLUE blood dots drift steadily along the band all film. On 'as the pace rises', the GREEN bar creeps up (still below the ceiling), MAGENTA dots seep from the muscle into the band and the gauge fill rises, slowly, then faster. On the question, large YELLOW text across the top: 'Is oxygen running out?'

Title 'The Balance Behind the Bend' fades in for two seconds above the world while the question text fades out. BLUE dots keep drifting; a few MAGENTA dots keep seeping into the band; the gauge holds.

scenes.tts: A 2008 review names three things behind endurance. The ceiling itself. The fraction of it a person can sustain. And economy, the oxygen cost of moving at a given speed. That fraction is related to the lactate threshold.
scenes.narration: A 2008 review names three things behind endurance. The ceiling itself. The fraction of it a person can sustain. And economy, the oxygen cost of moving at a given speed. That fraction is related to the lactate threshold.
scenes.caption: A 2008 review names three things behind endurance. The ceiling itself. The fraction of it a person can sustain. And economy, the oxygen cost of moving at a given speed. That fraction is related to the lactate threshold.
scenes.visual: The GREEN uptake bar slides to the centre and grows to fill about 65% of the frame height; the muscle, band and gauge dim but keep moving behind it. Three large labels attach to it in turn: on 'the ceiling itself', the YELLOW dashed line pulses, label 'ceiling'; on 'the fraction', a bracket from the bar's floor to its 'race pace' level, label 'fraction sustained' (schematic, no percentage); on 'economy', a small GREEN cost chip beside a speed arrow, label 'oxygen cost per speed'. Small tag top left: 'Joyner and Coyle, review'. On 'lactate threshold', the 'fraction sustained' bracket glows and a thin WHITE link line runs from it to the gauge, labelled 'lactate threshold'. The bar then slides back to the left edge.

scenes.tts: To see that threshold, start with lactate. It is a fuel, not waste. Some pyruvate from glycolysis becomes lactate and leaves the fibres that make it. Other fibres and the heart burn it, and the liver makes glucose from it.
scenes.narration: To see that threshold, start with lactate. It is a fuel, not waste. Some pyruvate from glycolysis becomes lactate and leaves the fibres that make it. Other fibres and the heart burn it, and the liver makes glucose from it.
scenes.caption: To see that threshold, start with lactate. It is a fuel, not waste. Some pyruvate from glycolysis becomes lactate and leaves the fibres that make it. Other fibres and the heart burn it, and the liver makes glucose from it.
scenes.visual: Back to the full world. On 'not waste', a GREY trash-can icon appears beside the muscle, gets a RED cross and fades. On 'leaves the fibres', MAGENTA dots stream out of the PURPLE muscle into the BLUE band. Downstream, at the RIGHT end of the band, three takers appear in turn and stay all film: a small PURPLE block 'other fibres', a BLUE heart 'heart', a brown liver shape 'liver'. On 'burn it', MAGENTA dots enter the fibre block and the heart and wink out with a small flash; on 'into glucose', dots enter the liver and leave it as TEAL dots back into the band. Labels only; no chemical structures.

scenes.tts: How much fuel is that? In one tracer study of twelve trained and untrained men, blood lactate supplied an estimated third of carbohydrate energy. That was over sixty minutes at the lactate threshold.
scenes.narration: How much fuel is that? In one tracer study of 12 trained and untrained men, blood lactate supplied an estimated third of carbohydrate energy. That was over 60 minutes at the lactate threshold.
scenes.caption: How much fuel is that? In one tracer study of 12 trained and untrained men, blood lactate supplied an estimated third of carbohydrate energy. That was over 60 minutes at the lactate threshold.
scenes.visual: A large TEAL ring appears above the takers, labelled 'carbohydrate energy'. On 'an estimated third', a MAGENTA slice sweeps one third of the ring (120 degrees), labelled 'from blood lactate (estimate)'. Small tag beside it: '6 trained, 6 untrained men'. On 'sixty minutes', a clock hand sweeps once around a small dial labelled '60 min at threshold'. MAGENTA dots keep flowing from muscle to takers below. The ring then shrinks away.

scenes.tts: So the lactate in blood is a balance. Here is the key idea. Blood lactate is set by the balance of appearance and clearance: how fast it enters, against how well it is removed. As work rises, appearance keeps rising.
scenes.narration: So the lactate in blood is a balance. Here is the key idea. Blood lactate is set by the balance of appearance and clearance: how fast it enters, against how well it is removed. As work rises, appearance keeps rising.
scenes.caption: So the lactate in blood is a balance. Here is the key idea. Blood lactate is set by the balance of appearance and clearance: how fast it enters, against how well it is removed. As work rises, appearance keeps rising.
scenes.visual: The gauge moves to centre and grows to about 60% of frame height. Two thick arrows attach to it: a MAGENTA arrow IN from the muscle side labelled 'appearance', and a MAGENTA arrow OUT toward the three takers labelled 'clearance'. On 'balance of appearance and clearance', large text under the gauge: 'appearance vs clearance'. When the arrows are equal width, the gauge level holds steady. A dial at bottom left labelled 'work rate' appears; on 'as work rises', its needle steps up three times and the IN arrow thickens at each step while the OUT arrow thickens too, by the same amount, so the level stays nearly flat (schematic).

scenes.tts: Now raise the work rate step by step. Appearance climbs with every step. Suppose clearance has already reached its peak and holds there. What does blood lactate do?
scenes.narration: Now raise the work rate step by step. Appearance climbs with every step. Suppose clearance has already reached its peak and holds there. What does blood lactate do?
scenes.caption: Now raise the work rate step by step. Appearance climbs with every step. Suppose clearance has already reached its peak and holds there. What does blood lactate do?
scenes.visual: The work-rate needle steps up three more times; at each step the IN arrow thickens by the same amount. On 'reached its peak', the OUT arrow stops growing and a small WHITE tag on it reads 'at its peak'. The gauge level is FROZEN: it does not move during this scene (do not show the answer). Question card across the top in YELLOW: 'Clearance flat. Lactate does what?'

Deliberate thinking pause. The YELLOW question card stays. The thick IN arrow and the thinner, fixed OUT arrow both shimmer; BLUE dots drift along the band; the gauge level stays frozen. No other change.

scenes.tts: It climbs faster, because appearance outpaces clearance more with every step. In one study of trained men, clearance did peak below the threshold. That fits the faster climb, but does not prove it causes the bend.
scenes.narration: It climbs faster, because appearance outpaces clearance more with every step. In one study of trained men, clearance did peak below the threshold. That fits the faster climb, but does not prove it causes the bend.
scenes.caption: It climbs faster, because appearance outpaces clearance more with every step. In one study of trained men, clearance did peak below the threshold. That fits the faster climb, but does not prove it causes the bend.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. A shaded MAGENTA wedge between the IN and OUT arrow widths labels 'the gap'; it widens with each work-rate step, and the gauge level rises faster at each step. As it rises, the gauge's top traces a curve onto a plot that unfolds to its right: x axis 'work rate', y axis 'blood lactate', GREY, no numbers, tag 'schematic'. The curve runs nearly flat, then bends upward. On 'below the threshold', a WHITE marker on the x axis labelled 'clearance peak' sits just left of the bend. Small tag: 'trained men, one study'. On 'does not prove', a RED tag 'fits, not proven' appears between the marker and the bend.

scenes.tts: That bend marks the lactate threshold: the workload above which blood lactate accumulation speeds up. It has no universal value. It is not a fixed four millimoles per litre, or a fixed share of the ceiling.
scenes.narration: That bend marks the lactate threshold: the workload above which blood lactate accumulation speeds up. It has no universal value. It is not a fixed 4 mmol per L, or a fixed share of the ceiling.
scenes.caption: That bend marks the lactate threshold: the workload above which blood lactate accumulation speeds up. It has no universal value. It is not a fixed 4 mmol per L, or a fixed share of the ceiling.
scenes.visual: The plot grows to fill about 65% of the frame; the gauge shrinks beside it, still linked. On 'lactate threshold', a WHITE dashed vertical line drops through the bend, labelled 'lactate threshold'. On 'no universal value', a second schematic curve (a second person, lighter MAGENTA) draws in, bending at a different work rate and a different height; its own WHITE dashed line appears. On 'four millimoles', a GREY dashed horizontal line labelled '4 mmol/L?' crosses both curves away from both bends; a RED cross strikes the '?' label. On 'share of the ceiling', a small YELLOW tag '% of ceiling?' appears and is struck the same way. Everything schematic: no axis numbers.

scenes.tts: Nor is it where oxygen runs out. Above the threshold, muscle keeps consuming oxygen and burning fuel. Lactate is still cleared and still burned. Only the balance has tipped.
scenes.narration: Nor is it where oxygen runs out. Above the threshold, muscle keeps consuming oxygen and burning fuel. Lactate is still cleared and still burned. Only the balance has tipped.
scenes.caption: Nor is it where oxygen runs out. Above the threshold, muscle keeps consuming oxygen and burning fuel. Lactate is still cleared and still burned. Only the balance has tipped.
scenes.visual: The second curve fades; the plot shrinks back to the right and the full world returns. Work-rate needle above the threshold mark. On 'consuming oxygen', a short BLUE inflow appears entering the PURPLE muscle from the left (blood still flowing left to right), and small GREEN oxygen dots ride it into the muscle and keep entering it steadily; the GREEN uptake bar at the left edge rises a little further, still below the YELLOW ceiling. On 'still cleared', MAGENTA dots keep entering the three takers and winking out. On 'balance has tipped', the IN arrow is visibly thicker than the OUT arrow and the gauge keeps rising. The YELLOW opening question 'Is oxygen running out?' reappears briefly and is answered with a large 'No'.

scenes.tts: The same study compared trained and untrained men. At each group's own threshold, clearance was thirty-four percent higher in the trained men. Comparing groups shows an association, not cause.
scenes.narration: The same study compared trained and untrained men. At each group's own threshold, clearance was 34 percent higher in the trained men. Comparing groups shows an association, not cause.
scenes.caption: The same study compared trained and untrained men. At each group's own threshold, clearance was 34 percent higher in the trained men. Comparing groups shows an association, not cause.
scenes.visual: Two copies of the OUT arrow appear side by side under the gauge, labelled 'untrained' and 'trained', each tagged 'at own threshold'. The trained arrow is 1.34 times as wide as the untrained one (computed from 34 percent), label '+34%'. On 'association', a RED tag 'groups compared, not caused' appears between them. The two copies then merge back into the single OUT arrow.

scenes.tts: So the bend in the curve is a balance tipping, not oxygen failing. Lactate keeps flowing from the fibres that make it to the tissues that use it. Above the threshold, it simply arrives faster than it is cleared.
scenes.narration: So the bend in the curve is a balance tipping, not oxygen failing. Lactate keeps flowing from the fibres that make it to the tissues that use it. Above the threshold, it simply arrives faster than it is cleared.
scenes.caption: So the bend in the curve is a balance tipping, not oxygen failing. Lactate keeps flowing from the fibres that make it to the tissues that use it. Above the threshold, it simply arrives faster than it is cleared.
scenes.visual: Full world, wide. The small plot at right shows the curve with its WHITE threshold line. On 'a balance tipping', the IN and OUT arrows at the gauge rock like a balance beam and settle with IN heavier; on 'not oxygen failing', GREEN oxygen dots keep flowing into the muscle through its left inflow. On 'from the fibres that make it to the tissues that use it', one bright MAGENTA stream traces the whole path from the PURPLE muscle along the BLUE band to the other fibres, the heart and the liver. On 'arrives faster than it is cleared', the IN arrow pulses, then the OUT arrow, and the gauge level ticks up.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (BLUE blood dots drifting, MAGENTA dots flowing from muscle to takers, gauge rising gently). Large centred white text: 'Lactate builds when appearance outruns clearance, not when oxygen runs out.'
